readme.html:
2D Drawing → Priced BOQ

Drop in a construction drawing — a flat PDF, or a DXF for pinpoint accuracy — and get back a priced Bill of Quantities in Excel, organized by trade, with a HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW confidence flag on every line so your estimator knows what to trust and what to verify.

Covers architectural and structural — doors, windows, fixtures, finishes, columns, piles, walls, beams, footings, slabs, and reinforcement. No BIM model needed. Every number is traced back to the exact spot on the drawing it came from, so you can spot-check without opening the whole set. Runs on your machine — nothing gets uploaded anywhere.

Built by Hamza Jabbar · AutoConst

Who this is for

Estimators, GCs, subs — anyone handed a drawing set who has to produce a priced BOQ. Works whether the drawings label elements D-101, 210.1, 270A, Po-1, or any other house style, in English or French.

Two ways in — pick what you have

  • PDF (the common case): reads the hidden vector text — schedules, plan callouts, dimensions. Counts and schedule/label-based quantities come out HIGH; un-dimensioned members are flagged for verification. If you have a flat PDF, this is you.
  • DXF (the accurate case): reads the real CAD geometry — exact per-member lengths, slab areas, and block counts in real units, isolated by layer. Got the DXF/DWG from the engineer? Expect a high-accuracy structural takeoff. Ask for it — it's a 30-second export and it turns "verify" into "exact."

How to use it (the easy way — no coding)

You need Claude Code installed. That's it.

1. Clone this repo (one-time) Open Claude Code, and in its chat say:

Clone https://github.com/hamzaabduljabbar/autoconst-claude-2d-pdf-to-priced-boq into my home folder.

2. Install it as a slash command (one-time — works from ANY Claude session on your machine) Ask Claude:

Install the 2d-pdf-to-priced-boq skill: copy SKILL.md from the cloned repo to ~/.claude/skills/2d-pdf-to-priced-boq/SKILL.md.

Now /2d-pdf-to-priced-boq works from any Claude session.

3. Set up your rates (one-time) Copy rates/rate-library.template.csv → rates/rate-library.csv and fill in your prices. You can enter rates in any unit (sf, cy, lf, m2, m3, ea, ton, lb…) — the pricer converts automatically. Full walkthrough: docs/building-your-rate-library.md.

4. Run it — from any session, forever after Put a drawing PDF in inputs/, then in any Claude session type:

/2d-pdf-to-priced-boq

Or just describe what you want:

Run the takeoff on my PDF and produce a priced BOQ.

Claude finds the repo, runs the pipeline, and lands a formatted Excel BOQ in outputs/. Open it. Done.

No re-cloning, no cd-ing around. Once installed, it's a slash command.

What you get

  • Architectural counts — doors, windows, fixtures, luminaires, diffusers, panels — with real quantities pulled from schedules and confirmed on the plans. Full attributes on each (a door's room, size, fire rating, hardware).
  • Structural quantities — piles, columns, walls, beams, footings, slabs. Concrete m³ (from footing L×W×D or beam section+length), steel length and tonnage (a W18×35 name encodes its weight), pile/column counts with sections, and gross slab area from the printed overall dimensions.
  • Reinforcement — a rebar register (every N12-300, 4N16, #5, H12, HA12 callout parsed with the correct bar weight) plus a tonnage estimate from concrete volume × typical rate — the standard tender-stage method.
  • DXF = exact — feed a DXF and per-member lengths, slab areas, and counts come straight from the geometry in real units, all HIGH confidence.
  • Works in English and French — 500x220 r.c. column or Po-1 20x40ht (3.54ml), mm or cm.
  • Each element tagged with its CSI MasterFormat trade code, grouped into divisions (Concrete, Metals, Openings, Finishes, Plumbing, HVAC, Electrical…) in the Excel.
  • Priced with your rate library — nothing invented. Live =Qty × Rate formulas so your estimator can tweak.
  • Every line flagged HIGH / MEDIUM (verify) / RATE_NOT_FOUND (add a rate). Nothing hidden.
  • Every number is checkable in seconds. Ask Claude "show me door 270A" and it renders the schedule row and the exact spot on the floor plan as PNGs. You verify one image, not the whole sheet.
  • Tells you what it can't read. On load it flags any scanned/raster page that needs OCR, instead of silently skipping it.

What makes this different from commercial takeoff software

Bluebeam and PlanSwift make you click every element manually — hours per project. AI takeoff tools (Togal, Countly) claim automation but are opaque: you either trust the number or you don't. This tool is both automated and auditable — every number is a database query with a named source, and any mark can be shown at its exact spot on the PDF in two seconds.

  • No vision, no OCR — reads the vector text and CAD geometry directly, so it's deterministic, cheap, and can't hallucinate.
  • Two-witness rule — a count is only HIGH when the schedule and the plan agree on it. The same guarantee an IFC model gives you, rebuilt from a flat PDF.
  • Convention-agnostic, multilingual — any tag style (D-101, 210.1, 270A, Po-1), English or French, mm or cm. It uses the schedule's own marks to search the plans.
  • Honest about limits — a 2D count can't give a member's length without a printed dimension, so un-dimensioned members come back "verify" instead of silently invented. Want them exact? Feed the DXF.

What you need in the drawing set

Either a vector PDF (exported from CAD — if you can select/copy text in a normal reader, you're good) or a DXF (best accuracy). A scan-of-a-scan can't be read by any text-based tool — the tool flags those pages on load so you know they need OCR first.

For the PDF path, HIGH-confidence counts come from a schedule (door/window/fixture/panel…) or from labelled plan callouts (500x220 r.c. column, Po-1 …, P1..Pn piles). Sets with only unlabelled symbols are the hard case — you'll get MEDIUM counts, flagged for verification.

For the DXF path, you get exact geometry regardless of schedules — this is the route for structural sets that have no schedule but need real lengths/areas.

About the rates — important

This repo ships with no rate data. You bring your own. That's on purpose:

  • Legal — construction cost data (RSMeans, etc.) is copyrighted; we can't redistribute it.
  • Accuracy — your company's prices, or your region's, are always better than a generic average.

Format your CSV like rates/rate-library.template.csv. Sources you can use: RSMeans (if you have a subscription), 4BT OpenCOST, your state DOT's published bid data, your company's own price book. Full walkthrough: docs/building-your-rate-library.md.

You do NOT have to convert units. The pricer reads whatever unit you put on each rate (sf, cy, lf, ton, lb, or metric) and converts the takeoff quantity to match — so RSMeans $10/SF and metric $107.64/m² produce the same total. Cross-dimension mismatches (area rate on a length item) are flagged in the notes, never silently mis-multiplied.

Your rate CSV (rates/rate-library.csv) is git-ignored — it stays on your machine.

Real example — 89-page university project

Ran on an 89-page architectural set (46.9 MB, University of Rhode Island Bliss Hall) to prove it on a real project:

Result
Runtime ~2 minutes end-to-end
Doors extracted 147, HIGH confidence
Doors confirmed on plan 147 / 147
Fire-rated doors identified 48 (with their ratings — 45 MIN, 90 MIN…)
Vision / OCR calls 0
Manual clicks 0
Priced BOQ output one formatted Excel file, opened in Excel, ready to review

Every one of those 147 doors has: a room, panel type, width, height, finish, frame type, fire rating, and hardware set — pulled from the schedule, cross-checked against the plans.

Optional: use your own branded Excel template

Have a company BOQ template? Drop it in templates/boq-template.xlsx and tell Claude:

Run the takeoff and fill my template.

The tool auto-detects your column names (Sr No / Particulars / Unit Rate / Amount / …) and fills them in — keeping your branding, fonts, colors, and any formulas.

For the technical crowd

If you'd rather run the scripts yourself instead of asking Claude:

pip install -r requirements.txt

DXF path (exact) — one step, then price:

py scripts/takeoff.py dxf "PLAN.dxf" --db set.db     # exact lengths/areas/counts
py scripts/to_boq.py    --db set.db --out _q.csv
py scripts/classify.py  _q.csv _c.csv
py scripts/price_boq.py --quantities _c.csv --rates rates/rate-library.csv --out priced-boq.xlsx

PDF path (flat drawings):

py scripts/takeoff.py build      "SET.pdf" --db set.db        # + flags any raster pages
py scripts/takeoff.py schedules  "SET.pdf" --db set.db --auto # HIGH-confidence counts (~30s/page)
py scripts/takeoff.py dimensions --db set.db                  # concrete m3 / steel from schedule L/W/D & sections
py scripts/takeoff.py annotations "SET.pdf" --db set.db       # count inline plan labels (columns, piles, French beams)
py scripts/takeoff.py locate     --db set.db --include-numeric# find scheduled marks on the plans (any convention)
py scripts/takeoff.py reconcile  --db set.db                  # cross-check schedule vs plan -> promote MED->HIGH
py scripts/takeoff.py measure    --db set.db                  # gross floor/slab area from printed dimensions
py scripts/takeoff.py quantities --db set.db                  # recommended qty + confidence per type
py scripts/takeoff.py rebar      "SET.pdf" --db set.db        # reinforcement register + tonnage estimate
py scripts/takeoff.py cite       --db set.db --mark 270A --crop  # evidence: render the exact spot on the PDF

py scripts/to_boq.py    --db set.db --out _q.csv             # then classify + price as above

Re-run order matters — after re-running schedules, re-run dimensions → annotations → locate → reconcile → quantities. Full pipeline details, design notes, and tuning knobs: CLAUDE.md and SKILL.md.
